diagnostic_evidence.quote: with $\lambda_i u_i = 0$ and $\mu_i(u_i - C_{k(i)}) = 0$ such that

Applying complementary slackness yields the characterization in
Table~\ref{tab:kkt}.

issues.failure_explanation: For the minimization problem and the stated complementarity conventions, stationarity requires G_i-s_i rho=lambda_i-mu_i. At a lower bound, the printed equation instead forces G_i-s_i rho<=0, contradicting the table derived from it. For example, with N=1, y=1 and epsilon=10, u=0 is optimal because feasibility requires alpha=alpha*=t and the objective is 0.2t. Nevertheless, the printed stationarity equations require both rho>=-0.9 and rho<=-1.1. Thus the claimed KKT characterization is not necessary for optimality.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the right-hand side by lambda_i-mu_i and derive the table using that corrected stationarity equation, retaining b=-rho.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed KKT system and the claimed derivation of the table from that system are invalid; the table itself has the correct bound directions.
issues.title: The stated KKT stationarity system reverses the bound-multiplier signs
issues.why_classification: This is a local repair of the KKT premise. The table, working-set rule, updates and substantive optimization guarantees need not change.

issues.failure_explanation: The table implies max_Iup tau <= b <= min_Idown tau, not the displayed reverse inequalities. This matters precisely when there are no free variables and the endpoints need not coincide. With N=1, y=1, epsilon=10 and the optimal u=0, the endpoints are 0.9 and 1.1. The asserted inequalities require 0.9>=b>=1.1 and therefore exclude every valid bias.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the bound-direction inference to max_Iup tau <= b <= min_Idown tau. The midpoint convention can be retained.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed bias bound in the degenerate case is false. The midpoint formula itself remains valid when evaluated using the actual full-set extrema.
issues.title: The no-free-support-vector KKT interval is reversed
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the KKT inference restores the bound without changing the estimator, algorithm, parameter scope or convergence target.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
every free support vector $i$ (with
$0 < u_i < C_{k(i)}$) satisfies $\tau_i = -\rho = b$ at the optimal
solution.

issues.failure_explanation: KKT conditions at the optimum do not bound its multiplier using gradients at an arbitrary current iterate. Take the linear kernel, x=(2,1), y=(4,1), C=1 and epsilon=10. At initialization the stated interval is [1.1,3.6]. The full KKT optimum has alpha_1=alpha*_2=2.5, all other variables zero, and b=-1.4, outside that interval. This failure persists after correcting the separate reversed inequality in the no-free-vector remark.

failure_location.quote:
The optimal threshold $-\rho$ lies in the interval
$[\tau_{j^*}, \tau_{i^*}]$ (from~\eqref{eq:mvp} and Table~\ref{tab:kkt}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the asserted enclosure of the unknown optimal multiplier and describe these thresholds as a current-score heuristic whose decisions are checked by full reconstruction.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed enclosure cannot justify the shrinking thresholds as bounds on the eventual multiplier. The algebraic rewritings in the shrinking-asymmetry lemma remain valid, but the thresholds are only heuristic.
issues.title: Current MVP scores do not necessarily enclose the final optimal bias
issues.why_classification: A genuine enclosure must be weakened to a heuristic estimate. This is a limited loss because the shrinking method already includes full-gradient verification and does not require new global solver architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
$\Aactive \subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ denote the active set of training-point
indices
Free variables ($0 < u_i < C_{k(i)}$) are never frozen.

issues.failure_explanation: The tests concern individual dual variables, but a successful test removes both variables of a training point. No joint-eligibility rule is specified. For N=2, Omega=I, y=(1,3), C=1, epsilon=10 and n_check=n_min=1, the first update gives alpha_2=alpha*_1=0.8 and tau=(1.7,1.9,1.9,2.5). The zero alpha_1 satisfies the first freezing test, and the zero alpha*_2 satisfies the third. Removing their training indices also removes both free partners and leaves the active set empty, so the next argmax and argmin are undefined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Increment a training-point counter only when both associated dual variables are at bounds and both relevant freezing tests pass; otherwise reset it. Remove a point only under this joint eligibility condition.
issues.overall_effect: The stated shrinking procedure does not preserve its no-free-variable-freezing invariant and can fail before reaching the reconstruction safeguard.
issues.title: Training-point shrinking can remove a free partner and empty the working set
issues.why_classification: A short local change to the eligibility test resolves the granularity mismatch while preserving the method, correctness target and stated per-iteration operation counts.

issues.failure_explanation: The only loop has already ended when this branch is executed; there is no outer loop to continue. The branch is genuinely reachable without shrinking: with Omega=I, y=(1,4,5), C=1, epsilon=10 and maxiter=1, the first update leaves full violation 0.8. Thus the pseudocode does not define how to proceed on an allowed input requiring further optimization.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add an explicit outer shrinking-cycle loop around the iteration pass and reconstruction, exiting only after the full check passes, and specify maxiter as the per-pass limit. A hard global budget would instead require a separate nonconverged exit.
issues.overall_effect: The complete algorithm lacks executable restart behavior after failed full-set certification, including ordinary iteration-limit exits.
issues.title: The reconstruction failure branch has no enclosing restart loop
issues.why_classification: The surrounding prose already specifies the intended reconstruction/reactivation policy. Making that policy explicit in the control flow is a local repair rather than a new optimization method.

issues.failure_explanation: Reconstruction computes the full violation but never reassigns i* and j*. They can be outdated after the last update or selected only over a shrunken set. A concrete no-shrinking example is y=(1,2,2), Omega=diag(0,0.65,0.1), C=0.02, epsilon=10, tolerance 0.01 and maxiter=2, choosing alpha_2 in the initial tie. The two updates end at the exact optimum alpha=(0,1,1), alpha*=(2,0,0), with no free variables. The full bias interval is [1.1,1.15], but the stored last pair has scores 1.7 and 1.1, so the algorithm returns b=1.4, violating KKT.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: After reconstruction, store the full-set maximum and minimum scores, or reassign their argmax and argmin indices, and use those values for the no-free-vector midpoint.
issues.overall_effect: Even an exactly optimal dual solution can be returned with an invalid primal bias and therefore an incorrect fitted model.
issues.title: The final midpoint can use stale rather than full-set extremizers
issues.why_classification: The necessary full scan is already performed. Retaining its extrema is a local correction with no additional asymptotic cost or loss of guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Algorithm~\ref{alg:smo} applies to m2
without modification after substituting $\Omega \leftarrow \Omega_s$
everywhere.

For $a = +1$ (even symmetry), $\Omega_s \succeq 0$
follows from the fact that $\Omega$ and $\Omega^*$ are individually PSD.

issues.failure_explanation: A PSD kernel does not make the reflected cross-Gram matrix symmetric or PSD. For the rank-one PSD kernel K(x,z)=(1+x)(1+z), training points 1 and 2, and a=+1, the construction gives Omega_s=[[2,2],[3,3]], which is nonsymmetric. Its printed pair-curvature formula gives 1 for p=1,q=2, whereas the actual quadratic curvature is 0. Consequently Pu is not generally the objective gradient used by the algorithm. The supporting PSD premise is also false even for reflection-invariant kernels: for the linear kernel, Omega*=-Omega. A reflection-compatibility hypothesis and a different PSD argument are missing.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the construction to PSD kernels satisfying K(-x,-z)=K(x,z), and prove positivity using the projected features (phi(x)+a phi(-x))/2 or the corresponding four-block Gram matrix. Under this condition both parity kernels are PSD; replace the false cross-Gram PSD argument and revise the odd-symmetry nonconvexity discussion.
issues.overall_effect: The unrestricted m2 replacement does not define a valid kernel or preserve the gradient and curvature calculations. In particular, the claimed even-symmetry convexity and inherited optimality guarantees are unsupported.
issues.title: The proposed m2 kernel need not be symmetric or positive semidefinite
issues.why_classification: The repair needs a genuine kernel-compatibility hypothesis and a contained positivity argument. It narrows the unrestricted kernel claim but preserves the stated RBF setting, both parity variants and the solver architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Gradient updates~\eqref{eq:tau-update} are applied only to $\ell \in
\Aactive^{\mathrm{ext}}$, reducing each iteration from $O(N)$ to
$O(|\Aactive|)$ gradient operations.

issues.failure_explanation: The number of reconstructions alone does not establish amortization: cycle lengths also matter. With r reconstructions over T iterations, the stated dense reconstruction work contributes O(r N^2/T) per iteration. Even one reconstruction can be comparable to all optimization work when T is of order N, or dominate a short pass. The source provides no lower bound on cycle length, and immediate stopping is allowed. Frequent active-set oscillation is therefore not necessary for substantial reconstruction overhead.

failure_location.quote:
The $O(N^2)$ reconstruction step
\eqref{eq:reconstruct} is executed at most once per shrinking cycle, so its
amortized cost per iteration is negligible unless the active set oscillates
frequently

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State reconstruction overhead as O(r N^2) in total and O(r N^2/T) per iteration, retaining it in the complexity accounting. Any negligibility claim needs an explicit sufficient condition on cycle lengths.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed negligibility of reconstruction, and the resulting suggestion that amortized iteration cost is governed only by the active-set scan and gradient update, are not established.
issues.title: Once-per-cycle reconstruction does not imply negligible amortized cost
issues.why_classification: A limited weakening of the performance claim is necessary. Accurate cycle-dependent accounting preserves the algorithm and its local operation bounds without requiring new global architecture.
